items.stem:
How many solutions does this system have?

$$\begin{aligned}  x + 3y &= 12 \\   4x + 12y &= 50\end{aligned}$$

options.text: Exactly one
options.rationale: The determinant is $0$ — the two equations describe parallel lines, so they cannot meet at a single point.

options.text: None — the equations contradict each other
options.rationale: The left sides are proportional but the right sides are not, so the lines are parallel and distinct.

options.text: Infinitely many — the equations describe the same line
options.rationale: The left sides are proportional but the right sides are not, so the equations conflict instead of coinciding.

steps: Compare the two left-hand sides: $(1, 3)$ and $(4, 12)$.
The second row is 4 times the first, so $\det A = 0$ and the rows carry the same information.
But the right-hand side does not scale the same way: 4 times $12$ is $48$, not $50$. The equations contradict, so there is no solution.
explanation.principle: A zero determinant means the equations are dependent; whether that gives no solutions or infinitely many is decided by the right-hand side.
hints: Is one equation a multiple of the other?
If the left sides are proportional, check whether the right sides are too.

items.stem:
How many solutions does this system have?

$$\begin{aligned}  2x + 2y &= 11 \\   6x + 6y &= 33\end{aligned}$$

options.text: Exactly one
options.rationale: The determinant is $0$ — the two equations describe parallel lines, so they cannot meet at a single point.

options.text: None — the equations contradict each other
options.rationale: The right-hand side scales by the same factor as the left, so the equations agree rather than contradict.

options.text: Infinitely many — the equations describe the same line
options.rationale: The second equation is exactly 3 times the first, so it adds no information.

steps: Compare the two left-hand sides: $(2, 2)$ and $(6, 6)$.
The second row is 3 times the first, so $\det A = 0$ and the rows carry the same information.
The right-hand side scales identically ($3 \times 11 = 33$), so the second equation is redundant and the solutions form a line.
